key_provisions_or_claims: Public trust in data use is improving, but concerns about accountability, data security and surveillance persist.
Trust in data actors is highest for the NHS (85%) and academic researchers (76%), and lowest for the Government (38%) and social media companies (33%).
Awareness of AI is nearly universal, but public associations with AI are dominated by negative concepts.
Six in ten adults used AI chatbots in the past three months, and seven in ten know little or nothing about how AI is trained.
Digitally disengaged people show lower trust and greater concern about data security and AI impact.
annotation.summary_en: Executive summary of the fourth wave of the UK government's Public Attitudes to Data and AI tracker survey (4,947 adults, 2024). It reports rising trust in data use but persistent concerns, negative associations with AI, growing chatbot use and low knowledge of AI training. It has no robotics content.
